title: The Old Man Who Lost His Horse
text:
Near China's northern frontier lived an old man skilled in reading signs. One day his horse ran away across the border into the land of the nomads. His neighbors came to console him. The old man said: how do you know this will not turn out to be good fortune?

Some months later the horse came back, bringing with it a fine nomad stallion. The neighbors came to congratulate him. The old man said: how do you know this will not turn out to be a misfortune?

Now there was a good horse in the family, and the old man's son loved to ride. One day he fell from the new horse and broke his hip, and he was left lame. The neighbors came to console him again. The old man said: how do you know this will not turn out to be good fortune?

A year later the nomads invaded in force. Every able bodied young man was called up to fight, and of those who went to the frontier, nine out of ten died. Because the son was lame, he was not taken, and father and son both survived.
lesson: Judge events slowly. A setback can open a door and a windfall can carry a hidden cost, so keep your balance and wait to see how things unfold.
people: An old man of the frontier (Sai Weng), his son
source: Huainanzi, Chapter 18 (In the World of Men)
caveat: The Huainanzi was compiled around 139 BC; the frontier man is a figure of the parable, not a recorded individual.
